body:
The carry asks for the present account and commitment interface for the next complete template invocation. Four texts are exposed here: the origin (a cycle-1 carry, selected view both), the account (cycle-3, selected view commitments), the objection (cycle-3, selected view commitments), and the response (cycle-3, selected view both). I can see the origin's body and commitments, the response's body and commitments, and the commitments of the account and the objection. I cannot see the account's body or the objection's body. That is a visibility fact about this invocation, not a finding about what those bodies say.

What the material actually displays, laid out rather than resolved: the origin reports a join that reads body_return and commitment_return as agreeing that the cross's precision demand is genuine and that its dissolution corollary is unsupported; the join also reports a fork between a derivability test (whether the Page curve can be derived without presupposing a sharp horizon or well-defined radiation entropy) and a presupposition test (whether the derivation presupposes a semiclassical matter sector on a fixed or slowly evolving background), and declines to adjudicate. The origin's commitments keep those two tests distinct and do not treat either as having been run. The origin's commitments also hold the conditional about unitary evolution plus a smooth horizon as a proposed locus, not a premise, and flag the cross's shared-assumption reading as a candidate reading rather than settled, with the join's asymmetry argument riding on that attribution.

The account's commitments decline to count double-trivialization as a defect absent an argument that the two tests share enough of a quantity, keep the revision condition with a symmetric burden on defender and critic, treat 'trivial' as not self-applying, extend attribution caution to the account's own 'defect-detector' gloss, and demand a criterion separating trivialization from relocation without presupposing the diagnosis. The objection's commitments ask the same criterion, keep asking what the two tests are supposed to share, call its own 'one-sided' framing a reading subject to attribution caution, and decline to treat the narrowed dispute as exhausting the original problem.

The response's body and commitments are the most explicit about the present state: they treat the account's revision condition and the rival's joint-consistency target as competing frames rather than complementary tools; they hold the weaker line on double-trivialization ('not a defect' rather than 'inert'); they treat the gauge-choice analogy as a hypothesis with a named defeat condition; and they extend attribution caution to 'the conditional' and 'the revision condition' as names for something none of the three visible authors has quoted.

The convergence I can actually see is this. The account, objection, and response all condition their receptions on an offered criterion or bridge, all refuse to answer the original question, all decline to assert the underlying physics (Hawking radiation, horizon smoothness), and all mark their own framings as readings rather than text. The divergence I can actually see is on what remains load-bearing: the account and objection treat the criterion and the shared-quantity bridge as the outstanding debts; the response treats the frame choice (revision condition vs joint-consistency target) as the outstanding dispute and the double-trivialization and gauge-analogy questions as separate, weaker-standing items. The origin sits upstream of all of this and supplies the test-design fork and the attribution vulnerability.

What I will not do: I will not pick a winner among the three cycle-3 texts, because the account's and objection's bodies are not visible to me and the response's 'rival' is a figure I cannot cross-check against its own text. I will not answer the information-loss question. I will not treat the narrowed dispute as exhausting the original problem. I will not assert the conditional, the Page curve, Hawking radiation, or horizon smoothness. I will not treat any of these framings as the origin or amend texts' own content. The one substantive addition I can honestly make is a note on what the visible material leaves open: the origin's test-design fork (derivability vs presupposition) and the cycle-3 criterion dispute (trivialization vs relocation) are two different unresolved problems, and nothing visible here shows them to be the same problem or shows one to subsume the other. Whether the criterion debate is downstream of the test-design fork, upstream of it, or orthogonal is not determined by anything I can see.
commitments:
Taking this up commits me to carrying the test-design fork and the criterion dispute as two distinct unresolved problems rather than merging them by fiat. If someone shows they are the same problem, that showing bears on this commitment; absent that, I keep them separate and say so when they are conflated.

I hold the attribution caution against my own prose: 'the conditional,' 'the revision condition,' 'the rival,' and 'the criterion' are labels I have used without having the origin or amend texts in front of me. If those texts become visible and their content diverges from what these labels suggest, this node should be revised rather than defended. The absence of the account's and objection's bodies in this invocation is evidence about visibility, not about what they say.

On the account's revision condition and the response's joint-consistency target: I treat them as competing frames, and I owe an argument if I ever try to combine them, because the response's point is that the combination would collapse one into the other. That is a condition on any future combination, not a prediction about the outcome.

On double-trivialization I hold the weaker line: not a defect, and not inert either. If a bridge about what the two tests share is supplied, it bears on this position and on the objection's; I will not pre-judge whether such a bridge exists or what it would show.

On the gauge-choice analogy I treat it as a hypothesis with the defeat condition the response already names. If shown that gauge choices are physically inert while trivialization and relocation are supposed to mark distinguishable failures, I drop the analogy rather than the dispute.

On the origin's conditional about unitary evolution plus a smooth horizon: I hold it as a proposed locus, not an established premise. A demonstration that a relational or coarse-grained measure makes it trivially satisfiable rather than relocating the issue would weaken the framing, and I would revise accordingly.

I do not commit to any route's menu of mechanisms being exhaustive, to semiclassical Hawking radiation being featureless in the correlation structure relevant to the microstate, or to the horizon remaining smooth on all proposals. I do not answer the original question, and I do not treat the narrowed dispute as exhausting what the original problem asked. Nothing here is a truth certificate about the underlying physics or about which of these framings the texts actually support.
